candidates.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
candidates.abstract: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

candidates.title: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance
candidates.abstract: We study the dynamics of an ensemble of $N$ two-level emitters undergoing collective decay at rate $Γ$ and collective incoherent pumping at rate $R$, confined to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder. Although the population dynamics are confined to a finite set of rate equations, their quantum-trajectory representation involves infinitely many pump-decay histories. We derive an exact finite continued fraction for the Laplace-transformed Dicke-state populations by resumming the infinitely many quantum trajectories generated by competing pump and decay processes. Our construction provides a physically transparent interpretation of the tridiagonal resolvent and extends to arbitrary permutationally symmetric initial states. In the strong- and weak-pumping regimes, we obtain perturbative transient solutions. We also identify exact relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables at balanced pump and decay strengths. Our solution provides a starting point for extending trajectory-based analytical methods to more general driven-dissipative collective systems.

candidates.title: The Spatially-Resolved Recent Star Formation History of the M81 Disk
candidates.abstract: The nearby M81 galaxy---a tidally interacting $L^*$ spiral disk---offers a unique perspective on the interplay of secular and external processes in shaping galaxy properties. We present the most detailed, panoramic map of M81's stellar populations to date, using archival Hubble Space Telescope ACS photometry from the ANGST survey spanning the full optical extent of its disk. From color-magnitude diagram fitting, we recover spatially-resolved star formation histories (SFHs) over the last $\sim180\,$Myr. M81's global SFH is remarkably steady in the last $\sim180\,$Myr with slight enhancements seen $\lesssim15\,$Myr ago. The average SFR surface density rises toward the center before falling off within the innermost $\sim4\,$kpc. The disk is also notably lopsided, with the eastern half having formed $\sim50\%$ more stars than the western half over the same area---a trend missed by FUV-based SFR indicators due to dust systematics. Finally, the long-term SFHs of both M81 and M82 point to a pericenter passage $\sim1\,$Gyr ago. By identifying M81-M82 analogs in the TNG50 cosmological simulation, we rule out the more recent pericenter times of $150-220\,$Myr predicted by some works, as such passages are inconsistent with M81's undisturbed SFH over the last $\sim180\,$Myr. With this work, M81 becomes only the third $L^*$ spiral---after M31 and NGC 6946---to have its SFH spatially resolved across large areas of its disk.

candidates.title: Continuum thermodynamics of chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures
candidates.abstract: We develop a continuum-thermodynamic model for chemically reacting, multi-velocity and multi-temperature fluid mixtures. Partial balances of mass, momentum and total energy are closed using a single entropy density depending jointly on the constituent mass and nonkinetic internal-energy densities. Its partial derivatives determine the constituent temperatures and chemical potentials. For the chosen entropy flux and separately treated volume deformation, the strengthened entropy principle yields a weighted Euler relation constraining the partial thermodynamic pressures. We construct thermodynamically consistent constitutive relations for viscosity, heat conduction, Maxwell--Stefan momentum exchange, thermal relaxation and nonlinear reaction kinetics. The baseline model includes thermo-diffusion and its reciprocal coupling; a fully coupled reciprocal completion is given within the stated isotropic co-factor class. An alternative formulation couples chemical conversion and energy redistribution through specified elementary processes. We identify the material functions required for closure and admissible shifts of constituent energy zeros. An ionization network with resolved electronic levels yields Saha-type ionization relations and Boltzmann excitation ratios under the stated detailed-balance assumptions, recovering the Saha--Eggert relation at common temperature. Competing electron- and heavy-particle processes can maintain stationary populations while transferring energy between groups at different prescribed temperatures.

candidates.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

candidates.title: Galactic Dynamics Drives Cyclic Star Formation in Dipole Dwarf Galaxies
candidates.abstract: Dwarf galaxies are dark matter-dominated systems that are sensitive to feedback and display bursty star formation histories. This makes them ideal probes of the processes that regulate star formation. This work investigates the timescales of star formation rate (SFR) variability in isolated dwarf galaxies using high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of $50$ dwarf galaxies drawn from the Marvelous Massive Dwarfs and Extended Marvelous Dwarfs simulation suites ($7.3 <$ \lmstar $< 9.1$). We measure star formation histories in $10$ Myr bins and characterize their variability with power spectral densities (PSDs). At the population level, the PSDs of both disk and non-disk galaxies follow a broken power-law, with a break timescale near $100$ Myr. Individually, our galaxies show both smooth and bursty star formation. A subset of disk galaxies show quasi-periodic SFR oscillations about their mean, which we refer to as cyclic star formation. The dominant timescale of these oscillations scales linearly with half-light radius and is approximated by the orbital period at that radius. Cyclic galaxies have Magellanic Spiral (Sm) morphologies and host lopsided dipole gas disks. In these systems, the bulk of the gas in the lopsided disk moves between its maximum and minimum distance from the galactic center, compressing the star-forming gas once per radial orbit and driving the SFR cycle. Cyclic star formation adds a narrow Lorentzian component to the PSD, peaked at radial orbital frequency of the disk ($\sim 200-500$ Myr), which is comparable to burst timescales inferred from observations.

candidates.title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
candidates.abstract: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events. Yet it remains unclear how well foundation vision models support these capabilities, particularly from a moving egocentric camera, which is a natural view for robots. To investigate this, we collect an annotated tennis dataset and train a suite of vision models on spatiotemporal tasks. Our dataset contains egocentric video synchronized with five allocentric videos, estimated global positions, labeled contact times, and annotated stroke types. We then evaluate seven prediction tasks from egocentric images: 2D ego player and 3D ball localization, future player and ball trajectories, forehand or backhand stroke anticipation, time to the next ego player ball contact, and 3D ball position at that contact. We compare image encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models with jointly trained prediction heads. The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.

candidates.title: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
candidates.abstract: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Parameters that cause such striking outcomes are at the focal point of catastrophe theory - a branch of bifurcation theory that studies degenerate critical points of a potential function. We present theoretical study of topological configurations of optical vortex rings in elliptic Gaussian beams, which change dramatically at specific beam parameters. We identify two types of catastrophes, cusp and butterfly, near which very small changes of elliptic deformations lead to complex topological transformations of vortex rings.

candidates.title: A flexible approach to high-dimensional clustering and classification using mixtures of finite mutually repulsive mixtures
candidates.abstract: We propose a novel approach for clustering that is later extended to classification. Our methods are based on an underlying determinantal point process (DPP) that generates sparsity and separation of location parameters in a mixture of finite mixture models specification. A key aspect is the assumption of a DPP conditional on the number of groups and a prior on this number, which results in a dynamic mixture of repulsive mixtures. The proposed model also involves a sparse tensor decomposition of the covariance function used to define the DPP, which is coupled with a separate mixture model employed to handle the intra-cluster correlation structure. Further computational enhancement in the high-dimensional case comes from exploiting a mapping from Euclidean space to the space of (valid) correlation matrices. A suitable posterior simulation scheme involving a modified telescopic sampler is developed. The resulting approach is seen to perform satisfactorily in simulated and real data examples.

candidates.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
candidates.abstract: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

candidates.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
candidates.abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We use population constraints based on data from the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0), as well as constraints from the O3 search for intermediate-mass black hole binaries, to forecast the number and masses of binary black holes detectable by LISA. Using the released GWTC-5.0 population posterior, we obtain $6.6^{+5.5}_{-2.2}$ expected detections with signal-to-noise ratio $>8$ in 4 years (median and $90\%$ credible interval). The alternative population models we consider use a broken power law with two or three Gaussian peaks for either the primary-mass distribution or a common mass distribution for both black holes. For the three-peak model with the common mass distribution, extrapolating from $300$ to $1000M_\odot$ roughly doubles the median expected number of LISA detections to $\sim14$. The upper end of its $90\%$ credible interval rises from tens to thousands of expected detections, although approximations may limit the reliability of the most extreme counts. For the reference GWTC-5.0 population, $39^{+22}_{-11}\%$ of the binaries detectable by LISA merge during the mission or within $10$ years after its end and are potential multiband sources. Essentially all of these mergers would be detectable by a reference Cosmic Explorer configuration if it is operating at merger. Ground-based measurements of the high-mass population can therefore inform both LISA forecasts and the prospects for observing the same binaries through inspiral and merger.

candidates.title: Improving cosmological distance measurements at high redshift using Lyman-Alpha forest BAO reconstruction
candidates.abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) measures baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the Lyman-$α$ (Lyman-alpha) forest and provides a robust probe of the expansion history in the matter-dominated era. Yet, non-linear structure formation broadens and shifts the BAO peak. To undo these effects, we extend standard Zel'dovich reconstruction, routinely applied to galaxy surveys, to the Lyman-alpha forest. We validate our methodology on large-volume idealized Lyman-alpha forest mocks painted on top of the \textsc{AbacusSummit} $N$-body simulations, using linear control variates to suppress sample variance and thereby reduce the error bars by a factor of up to $\approx \sqrt{50}$. In fully sampled periodic boxes, reconstruction halves the radial BAO damping scale and reduces the uncertainties on the radial ($\apar$) and transverse ($\aperp$) scaling parameters by $\approx25\%$ and $\approx15\%$, respectively. It also reduces the non-linear shift from $Δ\apar=+0.3\%$ to $+0.10\pm0.07\%$, while $\aperp$ remains unbiased. To make this approach readily applicable to observational data, we demonstrate the impact of a survey mask with a DESI-like density of $50\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. For this mask, we compare two approaches to estimate the displacement field: either directly from the Lyman-alpha forest or using an external tracer with a number density of $\bar n \simeq 10^{-3}\,h^3\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, such as Lyman-break galaxies and Lyman-$α$ emitters---both key targets for DESI-II. Both approaches give comparable gains and reduce the uncertainties on $\apar$ and $\aperp$ by $\approx 27\%$ and $\approx 10\%$, respectively, with mild improvements for futuristic high-density surveys with $160\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. Correspondingly, the figure of merit improves by factors of $1.66$ for fully sampled boxes, $1.65$ for a DESI-like, and $1.76$ for a high-density survey.

candidates.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
candidates.abstract: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.

candidates.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
candidates.abstract: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

candidates.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: real-time algorithms
candidates.abstract: When coordinating connected and automated vehicles at an unsignalized intersection, the crossing order and the vehicle trajectories must be decided jointly. For a fixed crossing order, the problem can be formulated conveniently in a bi-level form where each vehicle solves its own optimal control problem, whose optimal value is a function of its entry and exit times, and a coordinator optimizes these times subject to precedence constraints. We compute the first and second order sensitivities of lower-level problems, which are required to solve the upper-level problem, by means of algorithmic differentiation using the real-time software package \texttt{acados}. This implementation exploits tailored algorithms to obtain a computationally efficient implementation of the optimal coordination algorithm. We validate our implementation in numerical simulations that demonstrate both real-time feasibility and effectiveness of our algorithm.

candidates.title: Agentic Distributional Regression: Conditional Density Estimation through Agent-Written Programs
candidates.abstract: In this paper we propose a method for estimating conditional densities from an iid sample using a language-model agent. The agent writes the estimator as a short program that, for each covariate value, returns the estimated conditional distribution of the response. The program is built from a library of probability distributions, so the returned law can be a parametric distribution, a mixture or a multivariate factorization, with parameters given by explicit functions of the covariates. Since the number of operations and constants in the program is limited, the fitted conditional density is a formula that can be inspected and evaluated independently of the agent, while the choice of the model structure and of the fitting procedure is left to the agent. We call this approach agentic distributional regression (ADR). Treating the returned program as a random conditional density estimator, we derive a finite-sample error bound under explicit complexity and optimization assumptions, and an oracle inequality for selection using independent validation data. For a stably selected regular structure with sufficiently accurate fitting, we obtain asymptotic normality of the fitted constants. In simulation studies, on twelve real datasets and on a new dataset collected after the agents' training data, ADR with Claude Opus 5.5 has the best average performance among the methods considered.

candidates.title: Surface-Illuminated Interdigitated Ge-on-Si Avalanche Photodiode With Separated Ge Absorption, Si Multiplication, and Lateral Field Engineering
candidates.abstract: This work presents a surface-illuminated lateral Ge-on-Si interdigitated separate-absorption-charge-multiplication (SACM) avalanche photodiode for 1550-nm detection. The intrinsic-region spacing, P$^-$ charge-control width, and finger geometry are engineered to suppress high-field penetration toward the Ge/Si heterointerface and localize avalanche multiplication in Si. Simulations show that wider charge-control or intrinsic regions reduce fixed-bias dark current and shift avalanche onset to higher reverse bias. Among the tested structures, the intrinsic-region spacing/P$^-$ charge-control width of 0.5/0.15 $μ$m achieved a peak responsivity of 11.81 A/W at 1550 nm. At a -20 V applied voltage, it exhibited a multiplication gain of 3.796, a 3-dB bandwidth of 7.13 GHz, and a matched-bias gain-bandwidth product of 27.07 GHz. Optical-power-dependent measurements also show avalanche-gain compression consistent with space-charge screening. These results demonstrate effective lateral-field engineering for high-speed, surface-illuminated Ge-on-Si APDs.

candidates.title: Water at the molecular frontier
candidates.abstract: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinement and interfacial forces produce a range of behaviours absent in the bulk. Sometimes this amounts to a renormalization of bulk properties; in other cases, new and non-intuitive phenomena emerge - exotic phases, anomalous transport, and dielectric responses that defy continuum expectations. A convergence of atomically precise nanofluidic devices, novel spectroscopies and microscopy approaches, and machine-learning-accelerated simulations is now exposing the molecular mechanisms behind these behaviours. This Perspective argues that the recent findings should not be viewed as isolated nanoscale anomalies, but as evidence for a molecular regime of water in which continuum descriptions must be rethought and molecular-level understanding becomes essential. Recognising and exploring this regime should have consequences ranging from fundamental physics to the rational design of future technologies that rely on water and dissolved ions.

candidates.title: Little Red Dots with Broad H$β$ Lines Reveal the Black Hole Mass Function at 7<z<9.5
candidates.abstract: We present a systematic search for broad H$β$ emission at $7<z<9.5$ in 21,770 JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra drawn from four blank fields and six lensing clusters with photometry spanning 1942 arcmin$^2$. We find a sample of 20 sources with statistically significant broad-H$β$ emission, including 13 new sources. Our entire sample has colors and morphologies consistent with little red dots (LRDs), compared to only 37\% of broad-line emitters at $3.5<z<6$. Interpreting the broad-lines as indicators of Broad-line Active Galactic Nuclei (BLAGN), we infer black hole masses of $4.2\times10^{6}-2.1\times10^{8}$\,$M_{\odot}$. We calculate completeness corrections and construct the black hole mass function at $z\sim8$. The normalization of the black hole mass function rises by $\approx1.0$~dex from $z\sim8-5$, consistent with average black hole growth at $f_{\textrm{Edd}}\approx0.1$. Comparing with cosmological simulations, the $z\sim8$ black hole mass function requires heavy ($10^5$\,$M_{\odot}$) seeds or super-Eddington accretion onto light or intermediate mass seeds to match its normalization. Finally, we infer bolometric luminosities for the sample and construct a bolometric luminosity function. We integrate over this luminosity function to derive a black hole accretion density (BHAD) of $4.8^{+5.8}_{-2.6}\times10^{-7}~M_{\odot}~\textrm{yr}^{-1}~\textrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, showing broad agreement with previous photometric work, but disagreement with previous X-ray models, reinforcing the idea that BLAGN are more common in the early universe than previously expected.

candidates.title: TransGI: Real-Time Dynamic Global Illumination With Object-Centric Neural Transfer Model
candidates.abstract: Neural rendering algorithms have revolutionized computer graphics, yet their impact on real-time rendering under arbitrary lighting conditions remains limited due to strict latency constraints in practical applications. The key challenge lies in formulating a compact yet expressive material representation. To address this, we propose TransGI, a novel neural rendering method for real-time, high-fidelity global illumination. It comprises an object-centric neural transfer model for material representation and a radiance-sharing lighting system for efficient illumination. Traditional BSDF representations and spatial neural material representations lack expressiveness, requiring thousands of ray evaluations to converge to noise-free colors. Conversely, real-time methods trade quality for efficiency by supporting only diffuse materials. In contrast, our object-centric neural transfer model achieves compactness and expressiveness through an MLP-based decoder and vertex-attached latent features, supporting glossy effects with low memory overhead. For dynamic, varying lighting conditions, we introduce local light probes capturing scene radiance, coupled with an across-probe radiance-sharing strategy for efficient probe generation. We implemented our method in a real-time rendering engine, combining compute shaders and CUDA-based neural networks. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves real-time performance of less than 10 ms to render a frame and significantly improved rendering quality compared to baseline methods.

candidates.title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
candidates.abstract: 4D novel view synthesis (NVS) aims to render dynamic scenes across viewpoints and timestamps, which requires jointly inferring 3D structure and temporal dynamics. Existing monocular feed-forward methods often rely on explicit 4D Gaussian representations, which are prone to temporal inconsistency and severe rendering artifacts. We present FL4N, the first feed-forward latent 4D NVS model. Instead of relying on explicit 4D primitives, FL4N encodes a 4D scene prior into a unified latent representation across space and time. Our core insight is that learning temporal dynamics as residuals on top of a pretrained static latent prior enables effective 4D modeling with limited dynamic training data. To this end, we introduce a lightweight dynamic encoder that leverages static scene features to disentangle object motion from camera-induced parallax. Trained solely with an image synthesis objective, FL4N achieves state-of-the-art 4D NVS quality while rendering in real time. Its learned latent representation generalizes to real-world videos and disentangles viewpoint from time.

candidates.title: Differentiable Contact Dynamics for Legged Locomotion: Policy Learning and Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion. The exact contact sensitivity is available in closed form but describes changes within the current contact mode, providing no first-order information toward neighboring contact modes. The proposed gradient replaces this sensitivity only in the backward pass, leaving the hard-contact forward solve unchanged and the realized rollout feasible. A central-path relaxation of the de Saxcé-corrected second-order-cone complementarity problem for Coulomb friction smooths the conditions defining the separating, clamping, and sliding modes. The relaxed sensitivity is evaluated at a point on the central path obtained by a Newton iteration initialized from the hard-contact solution. The sensitivity remains continuous through contact-mode transitions and converges to the exact sensitivity as the relaxation vanishes. Using 100,000 samples and less than 2 min of training on a desktop PC, policy learning with the proposed gradient produces a policy that transfers to hardware without fine-tuning. On hardware, the robot under a trotting policy withstands pushes and traverses debris and slippery ground. In trajectory optimization, the proposed gradient reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients. Project page: https://diffcontact.github.io

candidates.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
candidates.abstract: The interaction of strong ($a_0>1$), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by $\varepsilon_{\rm B}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm B}/ω_0$, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For $\varepsilon_{\rm B}<1$ the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency $Ω_{\rm B}$ to scattering; when $Ω_{\rm B}$ exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm p}^{-2/3}$ to $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm B}^{1/2}/\varepsilon_{\rm p}$ wavelengths ($\varepsilon_{\rm p}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm p}/ω_0$; $ω_{\rm p}$ is the plasma frequency). When $a_0^2>\varepsilon_{\rm B}>1$, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.

candidates.title: Sparse Carleman Embeddings for Nonlinear Discrete Dynamical Systems
candidates.abstract: Discrete nonlinear dynamical systems arise in population models, iterative optimization, and numerical simulations, where computing many iterations can be costly in high dimensions. We study Carleman embedding for forced quadratic discrete systems and its application to quantum state preparation. Under explicit stability and initial-state assumptions, we prove that the truncation error decreases geometrically with the embedding degree, uniformly over all iterations. A central obstacle in discrete time is that the lifted update can become dense even when the original coefficient maps are sparse. We overcome this obstacle by constructing an exact auxiliary linear-system representation that applies the coefficient maps one tensor factor at a time, with row and column sparsities bounded independently of the truncation degree. After rescaling, the associated history system has a condition number that grows linearly with the iteration count, uniformly in the truncation degree. These results yield a quantum algorithm for preparing an approximation to the normalized $n$th iterate with constant success probability. Under coherent input-access assumptions, and for fixed sparsity, stability parameters, and a known positive lower bound on the final-state norm, the oracle query complexity is linear in $n$ and polylogarithmic in the inverse accuracy. Numerical experiments in one and three dimensions illustrate the convergence of the truncated embedding.

candidates.title: World Model for Energy Efficiency Maximization in Dynamic Metasurface Antennas
candidates.abstract: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) have emerged as a promising technology for realizing large-scale antenna arrays in next-generation wireless networks owing to their ability to enable dense and energy-efficient antenna architectures. However, jointly optimizing digital beamforming and DMA element weights under time-varying channel conditions remains challenging due to their coupled effects on the received signal and interference powers. We formulate this problem to maximize time-averaged energy efficiency (EE) under time-varying channel conditions, subject to transmit power constraints, Lorentzian phase limitations, and minimum rate requirements. To enable long-term planning and improve sample efficiency compared with model-free reinforcement learning, we develop a world model framework that learns latent system dynamics from interactions with the environment and jointly optimizes digital beamforming and DMA element weights through imagined trajectories. Furthermore, we incorporate feasibility-preserving action mappings and safety cost signals to ensure constraint satisfaction during policy learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the time-averaged EE by approximately 20% compared with the deep Q-network baseline, while achieving higher sample efficiency and more reliable constraint satisfaction.

candidates.title: The Impact of Flyby Interactions on the Rotation of Open Clusters
candidates.abstract: The Gaia astrometric mission has provided the first evidence for the bulk rotation of open clusters. While this rotation may arise from residual spin inherited from a cluster's parent molecular cloud, it is unclear whether this explanation always suffices, as angular momentum is carried away by escaping stars on the timescale of two-body relaxation. In particular, the recent observance of significant rotation ($v_{\rm rot} = 0.81 \pm 0.06$ km s$^{-1}$) in the dynamically old ($\approx 4$ Gyr) open cluster M67 motivates a study of another potential source of spin for Solar neighborhood clusters: tidal torquing from gravitational encounters with passing giant molecular clouds (GMCs). We derive an analytic estimate for the change in angular momentum of a cluster due to an impulsive interaction with a passing GMC, and verify this expectation by performing $N$-body simulations over a range of encounter parameters using REBOUND. For highly energetic encounters, significant angular momentum can be transferred, but the stars that receive the most angular momentum are ejected, leaving the cluster remnant with negligible net rotation. Even when considering a random walk of many GMC-cluster encounters, the integrated effects of these interactions cannot explain observations of dynamically old rotating open clusters. However, we find that within $\sim 5$ Myr post-encounter, some disrupted clusters could be confused as rotating clusters while their stars are still dispersing. Using the local density of GMCs, we estimate that up to $\approx 1\%$ of open clusters in the Milky Way may carry this faux-rotation signal.

candidates.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.

candidates.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
candidates.abstract: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.

candidates.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
candidates.abstract: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be thoroughly evaluated. In this report, we evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench as the core of an agent that controls a robot through an agent harness under the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained policies. We study two agent configurations: direct control, in which the agent generates waypoint commands directly, and harness with policy, in which it can also invoke a post-trained VLA or WAM policy for action execution. Under direct control, the agent achieves competitive overall performance relative to post-trained policies. It leads on short-horizon tasks and exhibits the least performance variation across generalization dimensions, whereas it underperforms post-trained policies on long-horizon tasks, tabletop manipulation, and high-precision contact-rich tasks. In the harness with policy, invoking a post-trained VLA or WAM combines the complementary strengths of both components, raising overall task success to the level of the strongest compared post-trained policies while substantially reducing token cost. However, performance remains below the per-task upper bound of the standalone components due to suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, and grasp disruption when the agent resumes control. Overall, our study characterizes the capability boundary of a frontier MLLM agent and suggests directions for improving future agent harness design. Project page: https://internrobotics.github.io/EBench-Astra-Tech-Report/

candidates.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
candidates.abstract: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.

candidates.title: An Ab Initio Quantum-Chemistry-Based Three-Temperature Approach for Non-Equilibrium Hypersonic Flows: Application to Homogeneous 0-D Chemical Systems
candidates.abstract: This work presents an ab initio quantum-chemistry-based one-bin, three-temperature (1-bin 3T) model for non-equilibrium thermochemistry of homogeneous chemical systems in their electronic ground state, derived using the multi-group maximum-entropy principle. The proposed framework captures both vibrational and rotational non-equilibrium effects, thereby enabling an accurate representation of thermochemical behavior in high-temperature gases. To account for departures from equilibrium dissociation, a non-equilibrium correction factor derived from ro-vibrational State-to-State (StS) analysis is incorporated into the population distribution. Because this correction is constructed from the quasi-steady-state (QSS) distribution, the resulting model is valid only for systems and conditions under which the QSS assumption holds. The proposed 1-bin 3T model is validated across a broad range of zero-dimensional test cases through comparisons with high-fidelity StS simulations and Direct Molecular Simulations (DMS). The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the reduced-order model and high-fidelity approaches for both dissociating and recombining environments. Overall, the 1-bin 3T model shows strong potential as an efficient and accurate framework for modeling non-equilibrium thermochemical behavior, while keeping computational costs orders of magnitude lower than the high fidelity ro-vibrational StS simulations.

candidates.title: Quantum Field Theory on the Tangent Bundle
candidates.abstract: We develop a quantum-field-theoretical framework on the tangent bundle in which gravitational and internal gauge structures are associated with different sectors of an affine tangent-fiber geometry. The translational sector supplies the coframe and its relation to teleparallel gravity. A reduced vertical spectral problem is based on the centrally extended Euclidean group \(E^{c}(2)\), motivated by projective representations of the stabilizer of a nonzero null vector. Twofold multiplicities of equivalent vertical representations in selected left-chiral sectors admit weak \(SU(2)\) actions, while an assumed threefold quark multiplicity admits a locally gauged color \(SU(3)_c\) symmetry. A proposed global quotient correlates the color center with vertical rotations on a threefold rotation cover. Together with the selected chiral spectrum and anomaly conditions, this construction reproduces the observed fractional quark charge assignments. We formulate matter and gauge-field quantization, BRST symmetry, and anomaly constraints. Under the stated projection assumptions, the color sector has the standard local QCD structure, including its one-loop beta function and asymptotic freedom. Additional gauge bosons and dark-matter states are proposed as hypothetical sectors. We also formulate a structural action for possible couplings between teleparallel torsion and additional Lorentz-sector potentials. The framework relates selected structures of particle physics and gravity within a common geometric setting; their further dynamical and phenomenological development remains open.

candidates.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
candidates.abstract: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,θ}$ boundary, $0<θ\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.

candidates.title: Recertifying decisions via e-closure: uniform improvements of conformal risk control and randomized e-BH
candidates.abstract: Statistical procedures often control expected loss at a prescribed level while leaving part of their risk budget unused. Building on the e-value representation of risk-controlled decisions and the e-closure principle for multiple testing, we formulate recertification, a general paradigm for improving procedures by exploiting computable slack in their validity certificates. A valid procedure's losses normalized by their risk budgets form a state-indexed e-value collection; conversely, decisions whose normalized losses are bounded by this collection inherit its risk guarantees. Recertification uses distributional structure to quantify slack, enlarge the certifying e-values while preserving validity, and construct less conservative decisions. We develop two applications. For conformal risk control (CRC) with a known loss family, recertification redistributes unused risk budget among the held-out points of each hypothetical augmented sample. The resulting controller is valid under every finite exchangeable law and no more conservative than CRC on any calibration sample. For convex losses on an interval of actions, repeated recertification converges geometrically to an admissible controller. For false discovery rate control with arbitrarily dependent e-values, recertification exploits unused conditional budgets in randomized e-BH. It yields a closed-form randomized procedure whose rejection set contains that of randomized e-BH for every realization of the shared randomization and whose expected number of rejections is maximal subject to the same conditional budget constraints. Recertifying with the larger e-collection of closed e-BH gives a second closed-form procedure whose rejection set contains that of the first. Experiments on CIFAR-100 hierarchical classification and multiple testing simulations demonstrate improved budget utilization, informativeness and power over the baselines.

candidates.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
candidates.abstract: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot. Without any real-world robot data during training, ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness and outperforming the MolmoAct2 VLA (33.3%), while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. We demonstrate that ZAP also generalizes to completely new objects, goals, strategies, and language by seating a test tube in a rack (and choosing a different hole in the rack when prompted), handing a test tube between arms mid-air, drawing an X on a tic-tac-toe board, and playing chess. These goals and types of manipulation don't appear in our training data. Furthermore, ZAP also transfers to an unseen embodiment. On a single-arm Franka, ZAP reaches 55.9% on RoboLab-120, 4.9 percentage points ahead of the leading VLA/WAM baseline.

candidates.title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
candidates.abstract: Many academic disciplines (in particular, mathematics and the theoretical sciences) face difficult questions about how to adapt their practices to the rise of highly capable artificial intelligence (AI). Before AI, a well-written research paper with a strong theoretical result acted as a reliable signal that its authors understood their field in depth. Now that AI is widely accessible, such signals have become cheaper to produce. As a result, they no longer reliably sort academics by their level of understanding. This has direct consequences for academic hiring. The age of AI raises a question for each side of the academic job market. Should an early-career researcher invest in a deep understanding of their field, or instead use AI to build a longer resume with many papers? Should a recruiter favor applicants with fewer papers who pass an interview aimed at probing understanding, or insist on both publication volume and a pass? In this paper, we develop a game-theoretic model of this two-sided dilemma. We classify all pure-strategy equilibria that can arise in this game and use learning simulations to identify the behaviors that populations of applicants and recruiters may learn to adopt. Our analysis provides a framework for reasoning about how academic hiring can adapt to AI and for evaluating practices that preserve the value of deep understanding.

candidates.title: On the Nash equilibrium for a model of traffic flow
candidates.abstract: The paper consider a conservation law model of traffic flow on a highway, where each driver chooses an optimal departure time $τ^d$, based on a departure cost $\varphi(τ^d)$ and an arrival cost $ψ(τ^a)$. Nash equilibria are studied, where no driver can reduce his own cost by changing his departure time. The first results provide continuity estimates on the arrival time, depending on the distribution of departures. In terms of the ${\bf L}^1$ distance, we show that the corresponding map is Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$ in Lagrangian variables (labelling individual drivers), and Lipschitz continuous in Eulerian space variables. Concerning the regularity of the a Nash equilibrium, our results show that, when the total number of drivers is sufficiently large, a queue alway forms at the entrance of the highway and the corresponding traffic density contains a shock. Moreover, for any number of drivers (possibly small), we prove that for generic $\mathcal C^2$ cost functions $\varphi, ψ$ the Nash equilibrium solution still contains a shock. In the last section of the paper, assuming that the initial departure rate is not a Nash equilibrium, we consider an evolution equation for the departure rate, where each driver keeps changing his daily departure time in order to reduce his own cost. It is proved that this nonlocal integro-differential evolution equation admits a unique solution, globally in time. This provides some theoretical support to earlier numerical simulations, which indicated the dynamic instability of the Nash equilibrium and the possible existence of a chaotic attractor.

candidates.title: Fréchet Kriging for Metric Space-Valued Spatial Data
candidates.abstract: Spatial prediction of non-Euclidean data, such as probability distributions, symmetric positive definite matrices, and networks, arises in many modern applications. Such data are naturally modeled as elements of general metric spaces, where classical kriging methods that rely on vector space structure are no longer directly applicable. We introduce Fréchet kriging, a general framework for spatial prediction of metric space-valued data. Fréchet kriging replaces the weighted average in classical ordinary kriging with a weighted Fréchet mean, while the weights are determined by characterizing the spatial dependence structure through a generalized variogram. This construction allows the proposed method to preserve the intrinsic geometry of the response space without requiring an embedding into a linear space. We establish theoretical properties of the proposed predictor, including a surrogate optimality property and consistency under variogram misspecification for a fixed working variogram under suitable regularity conditions. Simulation studies for univariate distributions and symmetric positive definite matrices demonstrate favorable predictive performance compared with existing approaches. We further illustrate the practical utility of the proposed framework through applications to exceedance probabilities of daily average temperatures, joint probability densities of daily minimum and maximum temperatures, and inter-industry monetary flow networks.

candidates.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
candidates.abstract: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.

candidates.title: Maximal Orbital Entanglement from Non-Interacting Fermions
candidates.abstract: Orbital rotations are used in quantum many-body physics and chemistry to reduce the complexity of quantum states by compressing their correlation into a small set of relevant orbitals. In striking contrast, quantum information processing strives for the opposite: orbitals that maximize entanglement as a resource. Motivated by this, we prove that Slater determinants of $N$ fermions on a lattice of $d_A + d_B = d$ sites, although free of particle correlation, can carry up to $\min\{d_A, d_B, N, d-N\}$ ebits of orbital entanglement. Given enough particles and holes, this equals the maximum over all fermionic states. For arbitrary free states, we derive the maximal orbital total correlation in closed form for all bipartitions, the finest partition, and all partitions of up to five sites, using new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices. Taken together, these results turn mean-field states, the starting point of most many-body methods in physics and chemistry, into a viable resource for quantum information processing.

candidates.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
candidates.abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.

candidates.title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
candidates.abstract: Quantum-centric supercomputing (QCSC) approaches, such as sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), combine quantum processors with high-performance computers (HPC), offering a promising route toward solving challenging electronic structure problems. However, implementation of QCSC approaches to large active space calculations is constrained by the associated number of qubits, deep quantum circuits, sampling cost, and large-scale Hamiltonian diagonalization. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a distributed QCSC framework that decomposes complex molecular problems into parallel sub-problems requiring fewer qubits, shallower circuits, and reduced shot budgets. A physically motivated, two-step aggregation scheme then reconstructs the global solution: first, a computational bit assignment strategy optimizes a cost function to appropriately map local bit indices to global ones, yielding a mapped tensor product state (MTPS); second, an inter-fragment correlation recovery module restores missing cross-fragment interactions. Herein, we employ a multi-layered generative machine learning architecture, starting with utilizing the recently proposed physics-informed generative SQD (PIGen-SQD) as a distributed QCSC solver, followed by a secondary generative module to model configuration distributions and identify dominant sectors of the global Hilbert space. For water and formamide dimers, our method achieves up to $95\%$ reduction in the diagonalization dimension while enhancing energy accuracy by an order of magnitude over conventional SQD. Furthermore, application to the water hexamer ($\mathrm{(H_2O)_6}$) cage successfully decomposes a 120-qubit problem into six 20-qubit monomeric subsystems, and stitches the monomers under a dimeric approximation, demonstrating excellent agreement with the reference classical methods.

candidates.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
candidates.abstract: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or risk reproducing anomalous content. Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space. Given normal supports, a velocity field is learned through conditional flow matching over frozen patch tokens to transport Gaussian noise toward normal features. Along straight paths, a single recovery step using one evaluation of the optimal field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration. The operating time governs how strongly recovery modifies a query token. With no anomalous validation samples available for tuning, a normal-only Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion selects this time from the supports alone. Squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts yield anomaly signals for both dense localization and image-level detection. Across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot benchmarks on MVTec-AD and VisA, together with sample-shot evaluations on Real-IAD, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance against recent category-specific methods. In the 1-shot setting, image- and pixel-level AUROC reach 97.8% and 98.0% on MVTec-AD and 95.3% and 98.7% on VisA, with a 2.1-point image-level AUROC improvement over the strongest baseline on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/b-rbmp/Flownomaly.

candidates.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
candidates.abstract: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states. In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback. We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies. Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning. Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments. We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.

candidates.title: Robustness of Skyrmion-Mediated Magnetization Switching in Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (p-MTJs) to Material Disorder and Elevated Temperature
candidates.abstract: Transient-skyrmion mediated voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) switching is a fast and energy efficient way to magnetization reversal, but its reliability under realistic material disorder and thermal fluctuations remain unclear. In this work, we use stochastic micromagnetic simulations of a 100 nm perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction to study switching reliability under grain-scale variations in Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, easy-axis orientation, and intergrain exchange coupling. We find that switching remains robust under moderate disorder, with 100% switching observed in 10^4 stochastic simulations after pulse width optimization at both 300 K and 350 K. Increasing the temperature from 300 to 350 K shifts the optimum VCMA pulse width from ~475 to ~450 ps, indicating that an apparent reduction in switching probability at a fixed pulse duration can be primarily due to pulse detuning. In contrast, strong easy-axis disorder reduces the maximum switching probability even after pulse-width optimization, indicating degradation of the switching dynamics. We further show that, under strong easy-axis disorder a transient skyrmion still forms while the subsequent post-pulse dynamics fails to complete the magnetization reversal. Our study therefore establishes the distinction between recoverable reliability due to timing shifts and permanent disorder-induced degradation that simply cannot be recovered by pulse re-tuning. Finally, for no disorders but at room temperature, 100% switching is observed with 10^6 stochastic simulations with correct pulse shaping.

candidates.title: Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes for solid-state batteries: computational screening enabling high critical current density
candidates.abstract: Sluggish vacancy-mediated self-diffusion in lithium metal limits the critical current density (CCD) of Li anodes in solid-state batteries by promoting interfacial void formation during stripping. To enhance the effective vacancy concentration while preserving the bcc Li host, we screen 50 substitutional solutes using density functional theory (DFT) within a funnel based on automatic phase diagram construction, solution energies, solute-vacancy binding energies, and experimental solubility limits. Using an adaptation of the Lomer model for the dilute limit, we show that only Ag, Ge, and Cd solid solutions are predicted to reach $1~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ within their solubility limits. The thermodynamically estimated CCD of Ag at $\sim 9$ at.% reaches $\sim 4~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ at a theoretical capacity of $1522~\mathrm{mAh~g^{-1}}$. Migration barrier calculations indicate that the enhancement may be partially offset by vacancy trapping, necessitating further validation via molecular dynamics simulations. Notably, Hume-Rothery rules alone prove insufficient as prefilters, whereas machine-learning models trained on the DFT data can eliminate most unsuitable solutes early in the funnel and extend the workflow to related solid-solution searches.

candidates.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
candidates.abstract: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

candidates.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
candidates.abstract: Personal email agents decide, for every message, what it is, whether it is urgent, whether to draft a reply, create a task, or ignore it. Their error rate is rarely measured: the stored labels were written by the system itself. We present Foyer, a self-hosted personal inbox agent in daily use, and a measurement protocol (stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, pre-registered hypotheses, human labels in the agent's review loop) that yields ground truth before any training. On 739 real Italian/English emails labelled by the owner (231 unbiased, 500 adversarially sampled), we compare nine systems under thread-grouped cross-validation: the production keyword rules, a TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline, local typed decision models (Tev1, Nimble), a hosted decision model (Nimble v4-max), and hosted generative LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma 4 26B/31B). Four results. The production rules score 28% on message type against a 58% majority class: the field shown most prominently carried no information. With ~200 labels, logistic regression has the highest accuracy on every field (type 0.79, urgency 0.74, needs-reply 0.83, is-noise 0.90), though it never predicts the two rarest classes and is statistically tied with Gemma 4 on type; few-shot prompting does not close the gap. The sender's relationship (client, supplier, service) is recovered from other emails of the same contact with 98.6% accuracy where the contact has been seen, and is not inferable from a single message by any model: it belongs in the contact graph, not the prompt. Finally, accuracy is not the product metric: composed into actions, the most accurate system most often ignores emails needing action (18% vs 4% for the best LLM); a cost-chosen threshold on its noise probability halves that rate and makes it the cheapest system.

candidates.title: Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes
candidates.abstract: Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. Molecular surface coatings offer a scalable strategy to improve humidity tolerance and interfacial stability, yet there is limited understanding of the molecular-level factors governing surface interactions. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.

candidates.title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
candidates.abstract: Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. Since the numerical construction of a stratification factor typically involves approximation, we establish continuity results for the associated conditional expectations and, more generally, conditional distributions, and provide several counterexamples showing the limits of this continuity theory. Combined with density results for neural networks, our findings yield a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. We conclude with numerical experiments involving a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model, where the learned factors outperform all considered benchmarks.

candidates.title: Low-Complexity Wideband Channel Estimation for ISAC in Analog Millimeter-Wave Systems
candidates.abstract: Accurate wideband channel estimation is a key enabler for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In the narrowband scenario, the Transformed Spatial Domain Channel Estimation (TSDCE) method was previously shown to provide fast and accurate angle estimation with substantially lower complexity than conventional compressed-sensing approaches based on orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). However, wideband ISAC scenarios additionally require delay estimation, making joint angle-delay sparse recovery computationally expensive due to the multidimensional dictionary search. In this paper, we propose a wideband extension of TSDCE, namely TSDCE-TD, which incorporates time-domain support and decouples angle and delay estimation. Two variations are proposed for delay estimation: TSDCE-TD (Dict), which uses a one-dimensional delay dictionary, and TSDCE-TD (FFT), which applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) zero-padding interpolation. Path estimates are iteratively refined through successive interference cancellation and alternating angle-delay updates. Simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform OMP-based baselines under practical dictionary sizes, while achieving comparable performance at high-resolution settings with substantially lower computational complexity. Moreover, the angle-delay estimates obtained using the proposed approach enable accurate single-anchor indoor localization in a ray-traced environment, achieving sub-20 cm positioning errors and satisfying practical indoor positioning requirements.

candidates.title: Low-frustration block encodings by patch routing
candidates.abstract: Block-encoding has emerged as a core primitive in many quantum algorithms, including quantum simulation. In this work, we design efficient and extensible methods for generating low-frustration block encodings of frustrated lattice Hamiltonians built from repeated local interaction patches through a technique we call "patch routing".
